Yes, that feels right and safe. When I clicked "Delete bookmark," it didn't just vanish — it asked me plainly "Delete 'A field guide to ancient libraries'?" so I know exactly which one I'm about to lose, and it spelled out that my saved title, labels, and note go with it and that it can't be undone. And there's a clear way to back out. So there's no way I'd wipe something by a stray click, which is just what I'd want for something permanent.

Starting it from the details also makes sense — deleting is a deliberate act, so tucking it at the bottom of a bookmark I've deliberately opened, behind its own confirmation, keeps it out of the way of everyday browsing. Good safeguard.

One thing that permanence makes me think about: sometimes I don't want to *destroy* a link, I just want it out of my main view — done with it for now, but not gone forever. That's a softer thing than this permanent delete. Is there a way to just set something aside like that, separate from this destroy-it-forever action? Not asking you to change this screen — this is right for real deletion — just wondering if that gentler option exists too.
